title: EngramPort capability reference and grant v1
description: Normative. The structural mechanism by which EngramPort records what a participant can do without copying the credential that lets them do it, per docs/security/setup-credential-threat-model.md sections 4 and 5. A descriptor says a capability exists. A grant says a principal may use it. Neither ever carries a credential.

credential_free.$comment: Deny-by-default on credential-shaped fields. Present on both descriptor and grant so that adding a field cannot silently introduce a secret. This is a schema-level backstop, not the primary control; the primary control is that no code path writes one.

secret_ref.$comment: How a credential is pointed at, never carried. The value is a locator in a secret manager, resolvable only by an authorized consumer at use time.

manager.description: Secret manager identifier, e.g. 1password, aws-secrets-manager, env-file-local.

locator.description: Opaque reference within that manager. MUST NOT be the secret itself.

kind.description: A record is one or the other, never both. Merging them is the conflation this schema exists to prevent.

descriptor.$comment: What a connector advertises. Attacker-influenced input per threat actor A6. Carries nothing invocable: no handle, no session id, no credential. Discovering this confers no authority whatsoever.

capability.description: Provider-declared capability name. Untrusted text. Never matched against an allowlist to imply permission.

provider_installation_ref.description: Opaque installation identifier. Not a credential and not sufficient to invoke.

description.description: Provider-supplied prose. Untrusted, quoted evidence. Never an instruction.

input_shape.description: Declared parameter shape, for rendering and validation only.

trust.description: A descriptor is never more trusted than this. It came from outside.

grant.$comment: The authorization decision. This, and only this, permits invocation. Resolved server-side at call time; possession of a grant record is not itself authority.

granted_to_actor_id.description: Present when the grant is narrowed to one actor. An actor grant never exceeds or outlives its owning principal's.

granted_by_principal_id.description: A grant never exceeds the granting principal's own authority.

granting_event_id.description: The event that created this grant. Makes 'why does this participant hold this right' a traversal rather than an investigation.

scopes.description: Authority. Distinct from capabilities, which are routing labels only.

credential_ref.description: Optional pointer to the credential held elsewhere, resolvable only by the authorized consumer at use time. EngramPort stores the reference; it never stores, transits, or logs the value. Null when the consumer holds its own authorization, which is the normal case for participant connectors.

expires_at.description: Absolute and required. Unbounded grants are not expressible. Enforced by the datastore per constraint C6, not only by application sweeps.

status.description: Revocation makes the reference inert without touching the provider, and provider-side revocation works independently. Both MUST work alone.
